site.name: Making Magic, Distilled
site.tagline: Key points from Mark Rosewater's design column, in five languages, with a link to every original.
home.lead: Mark Rosewater has written Making Magic every week since 2002. This site distils the essays into their key points so you can learn the design thinking fast, then sends you to the original to read it properly.
home.progress: {done} of {total} Making Magic columns summarized so far.
home.how.1.title: Rules text, not book report
home.how.1.body: Each key point is written like a card: the principle up top, the Magic example that produced it below the line.
home.how.2.title: Five languages, one summary
home.how.2.body: Every summary is written in English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, and Chinese. Switching language switches the source link too, when Wizards has published one.
home.how.3.title: Always links home
home.how.3.body: A summary is a doorway, not a replacement. Every article carries a link back to the full essay on magic.wizards.com.
series.jumpHint: Pick a lesson to jump to it.
filter.note: The colour on each lesson is our reading of which slice of Magic's colour pie the principle belongs to. It's an interpretation, not Rosewater's.

about.title: About
about.body: This is an unofficial, fan-made study companion for Making Magic, Mark Rosewater's weekly design column at Wizards of the Coast. Every page here is a summary written to teach the key points quickly; the essays themselves belong to their author and publisher, and every summary links back to them. Magic: The Gathering and Making Magic are property of Wizards of the Coast LLC. This site is not produced, endorsed, or reviewed by Wizards of the Coast.
about.contribute: Summaries are plain JSON files in this repository. Adding an article means adding one file.
footer.disclaimer: Unofficial fan project. Not affiliated with Wizards of the Coast.
